limitations: Four selected source images, not a paced or full-coverage replay.
Reference and cache calls are sequential, with changing temperatures/frequencies; no causal speedup estimate.
A 13.5 MB source archive was transferred by ADB near the final call; these timings are not an isolated benchmark.
Observed ready wall includes diagnostic hashing/copies but excludes later captures/saves and suspension guards; not capture-to-pose latency.
Peak RSS was observed on a 16 GB board; it does not validate an 8 GB deployment or long-lived map.
No accuracy, map-cadence, queue, 30-minute or physical-camera acceptance.
Three fixed source-selected pairs, not consecutive raw frames or a paced replay; no full coverage or GT quality gate.
Five FP32 canonical outputs and saved FP64 graph matrices compare cache-on with the same-pair cache-off original model; no historical gold used.
Observed ready walls include diagnostic input hash and owned canonical copy/hash. Post-forward guards, graph snapshot/NPZ save and comparison remain outside these walls.
Tail tokens are not saved: ownership/identity/hash/unchanged statistics are checked as suspension metadata only.
Original parameter/source/checkpoint/SL4 binding and cleanup facts are verified as before-after metadata, without a board rehash or model reload.
SL4 projective graph/decomposed camera-to-world serialization is not independently optimized, decomposed or declared a metric SE3 trajectory.
Short AB/BA/AB is thermally uncontrolled; root reports one 13 MB source-archive ADB transfer lasting 1.348 s during the last B call. No timing ratio is claimed as causal cache speedup.
The experiment uses its frozen pre-cleanup source closure; it is not a regression of the later public core cleanup.
No 20 Hz/P95 100 ms/30-minute stability/8 GB or physical-camera acceptance.
